macro.title: Global financial crisis
macro.mechanism: Export orders and industrial output fell sharply; commercial vehicle traffic and port container volumes dropped through FY09 before recovering from late FY10.

macro.title: Commonwealth Games, Delhi
macro.mechanism: Large NCR road and metro capacity commissioned around the event; temporary restrictions and lane reservations during the Games period.

macro.title: Supreme Court ban on iron ore mining in Karnataka
macro.mechanism: Ore movement to Goa and Krishnapatnam collapsed. Heavy commercial vehicle counts on the Bellary-Hospet corridors and connecting highways fell steeply and did not recover for years.

macro.title: Goa iron ore mining suspension
macro.mechanism: Ore truck traffic on Goa state highways and barge movement on the Mandovi and Zuari effectively stopped; Mormugao port throughput fell heavily.

macro.title: Uttarakhand floods
macro.mechanism: Char Dham route highways washed out at multiple points; pilgrim traffic to Kedarnath and Badrinath fell for several seasons. A long reconstruction programme followed.

macro.title: Crude oil price collapse begins
macro.mechanism: Brent fell from about 110 to under 50 dollars by early 2015. Diesel cost dropped, road freight rates softened, and commercial vehicle utilisation improved.

macro.title: Diesel price deregulation
macro.mechanism: Diesel moved to market pricing, linking road freight cost directly to crude and the exchange rate from this point onward.

macro.title: Chennai floods
macro.mechanism: Highways and rail into Chennai cut for days, airport closed, port operations disrupted. A sharp one-month regional dip.

macro.title: Bharatmala programme takes shape
macro.mechanism: Large national highway development programme announced, driving the award pipeline and, over the following decade, substantial new parallel capacity on many corridors.

macro.title: Demonetisation, toll collection suspended nationwide
macro.mechanism: MoRTH suspended user fee collection on all national highways from 9 November to 2 December 2016. NHAI reported a loss of roughly Rs 1,238 crore against an average daily collection near Rs 51.6 crore. Road movement also slowed while cash was scarce.

macro.title: GST rollout
macro.mechanism: State check posts dismantled. Truck turnaround times improved materially, raising effective vehicle utilisation. Freight patterns reorganised around consumption centres rather than tax boundaries.

macro.title: E-way bill for inter-state movement
macro.mechanism: Created a national record of goods movement, and shifted some informal freight into the formal count.

macro.title: Revision of axle load norms
macro.mechanism: Permissible gross vehicle weights raised by roughly 20 to 25 per cent. The same load moved in fewer trips, so vehicle counts fell even where the volume of goods did not. Counts before and after July 2018 are not directly comparable.

macro.title: Kerala floods
macro.mechanism: State highways and NH stretches submerged, Kochi airport closed for two weeks, rail services suspended. Movement across the state fell steeply for a month.

macro.title: Kumbh Mela, Prayagraj
macro.mechanism: Very large pilgrim inflow lifted passenger vehicle counts on corridors feeding Prayagraj for the duration, with heavy restrictions on commercial vehicles in the approach zone.

macro.title: Cyclone Fani
macro.mechanism: Odisha coastal highways and rail links disrupted; Bhubaneswar airport closed. Short but severe regional traffic loss.

macro.title: Commercial vehicle sales downturn
macro.mechanism: A sharp fall in commercial vehicle sales through FY20 signalled weakening freight demand well before the pandemic began.

macro.title: COVID-19 national lockdown, toll collection suspended
macro.mechanism: Toll collection on national highways was suspended from 25 March and resumed on 20 April 2020. Movement fell to a small fraction of normal and recovered unevenly through FY21, with freight returning ahead of passenger travel. The sharpest break in any Indian movement record.

macro.title: Cyclone Amphan
macro.mechanism: Severe disruption across West Bengal and Odisha during lockdown, compounding the traffic trough.

macro.title: Farmers' protest. Delhi border blockades
macro.mechanism: Sustained blockades at Singhu, Tikri and Ghazipur pushed traffic off the NH-44, NH-9 and NH-48 approaches to Delhi for over a year. Several plazas on those approaches stayed open without charge throughout.

macro.title: FASTag made mandatory
macro.mechanism: Electronic tolling became compulsory at national highway plazas. Record keeping changed substantially from this point, so figures before and after February 2021 are measured differently.

macro.title: COVID-19 second wave
macro.mechanism: State-level restrictions rather than a national lockdown. Traffic fell again but less deeply than 2020, with wide variation between states.

macro.title: Coal supply crisis
macro.mechanism: Power plant coal stocks fell critically; railways prioritised coal rakes over other freight, pushing some cargo to road.

macro.title: Russia-Ukraine war begins
macro.mechanism: Crude and fertiliser prices spiked, lifting road freight costs. Trade flows reorganised, including discounted crude imports that raised tanker and pipeline-adjacent movement at west coast ports.

macro.title: Record wheat export surge then ban
macro.mechanism: A brief export boom lifted grain movement to ports, followed by an abrupt export ban that reversed it within weeks.

macro.title: Joshimath subsidence
macro.mechanism: Land subsidence forced restrictions on the Char Dham route and a pause on some construction, affecting pilgrim season traffic in the Uttarakhand hills.

macro.title: Cyclone Biparjoy
macro.mechanism: Kutch and Saurashtra highways and Kandla port operations disrupted; short sharp regional dip.

macro.title: Sikkim glacial lake outburst flood
macro.mechanism: NH-10, the lifeline to Sikkim, was severed at multiple points. Long-duration loss of the only practical road access, with repeated closures in following monsoons.

macro.title: Red Sea shipping disruption begins
macro.mechanism: Attacks on shipping forced rerouting around the Cape, lengthening transit times and raising container freight rates. Indian EXIM cargo timing shifted, affecting port-connecting highway and rail flows.

macro.title: Mumbai Trans Harbour Link opened
macro.mechanism: Atal Setu opened, redistributing movement between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai and reducing volumes on the routes it replaced.

macro.title: General election
macro.mechanism: The model code of conduct froze new announcements and contract awards. Gaps in the project record across this window reflect the freeze rather than a real slowdown.

macro.title: Wayanad landslides
macro.mechanism: Severe hill road loss in Kerala, with extended closure of local connectivity and a reminder of monsoon risk on Western Ghats alignments.

macro.title: Maha Kumbh, Prayagraj
macro.mechanism: Exceptionally large pilgrim movement over six weeks. Passenger vehicle counts on feeding corridors rose steeply while commercial traffic was restricted or rerouted.
